subject: كون_1:#2
detail: Standalone يَكُونُ does not express a plain present 'is' in MSA; it reads as habitual/future ('patience will be / tends to be beautiful'). Use a context that needs يكون (e.g. after أن/لن, or a habitual frame) or translate accordingly; the Bosnian gloss 'bude' also conflicts with the sentence 'je'.

subject: خلق_1:#4
detail: Using خَلَقْتُ for a person shaping clay is theologically delicate (the Quran reserves this usage for Isa by God's permission) and should be avoided for a learner; the Bosnian 'Oblikovao sam oblik' is a clumsy tautology and the English 'figure' differs from the gloss 'shape'. Replace with a sentence where the agent is God or a negated human claim.

subject: كفر_1:#1
detail: The Bosnian 'Vjernik ne poriče' is unnatural without an object and does not convey kufr; render e.g. 'Vjernik ne niječe (vjeru)' / 'Vjernik ne postaje nevjernik', and align the gloss.

subject: كذب_2:#0
detail: كَذَّبَ الرَّسُولَ means called the messenger a liar; Bosnian 'je poricao poslanika' is unnatural (and imperfective for a single act). Use e.g. 'Nevjernik je poslanika u laž utjerao' / 'proglasio lažljivcem'.

subject: أخذ_8:#0
detail: اتَّخَذَ with a single object means 'took/made for oneself'; 'The man took a friend' / 'Čovjek je uzeo prijatelja' is unnatural and misleading. Translate as 'The man made (took) a friend for himself' / 'Čovjek je stekao prijatelja', or use the two-object pattern.

subject: أخذ_8:#3
detail: 'They took a house' / 'Uzeli su kuću' does not convey اتَّخَذُوا بَيْتًا ('they made/took for themselves a house'); translate as 'They made themselves a house' / 'Napravili su sebi kuću' or use the two-object pattern.

subject: أخذ_8:#4
detail: 'She took a friend' / 'Uzela je prijateljicu' is unnatural for اتَّخَذَتْ صَدِيقَةً; translate as 'She made a friend (for herself)' / 'Stekla je prijateljicu', or use the two-object pattern.

subject: خلق_1:past:ana
detail: خَلَقْتُ (I created) is God's own speech in the Quran; a practice sentence would put invented words in God's mouth, and for a person it is theologically delicate. Decide whether this cell gets a sentence at all.

subject: أخذ_8:#5
detail: English "The man made himself a friend" is unidiomatic and can read as "built a friend"; use "The man took a friend" or "The man made a friend" (matching the Bosnian "stekao je prijatelja").

subject: خلق_1:past:ana
detail: خَلَقْتُ (I created) is God's own speech in the Quran; a practice sentence would put invented words in God's mouth, and for a person it is theologically delicate. Decide whether this cell gets a sentence at all.

subject: أخذ_8:#8
detail: اتَّخَذَ الرَّجُلُ صَدِيقًا is correct, fully vowelled MSA: Form VIII past 3ms with a single object, as in Quranic اتَّخَذَ خَلِيلًا. 'Made a friend' / 'stekao je prijatelja' is a natural rendering, though it loses a little of the sense of deliberately choosing someone as a friend. The English gloss 'took (for himself), adopted' and the Bosnian gloss 'stekao je' are both acceptable. Nothing theologically sensitive.

subject: وكل_5:past:nahnu

Needs a person to choose. Candidate: تَوَكَّلْنَا وَبَدَأْنَا مَشْرُوعَنَا الْجَدِيدَ — We put our trust (in God) and started our new project. / Pouzdali smo se (u Allaha) i počeli naš novi projekat.

subject: وحي_4:#4
detail: Bare 'أَوْحَيْنَا لَهُ' is the iconic Quranic divine first-person 'We revealed to him' (أوحينا إليه); nothing in the sentence anchors a human speaker, so it can read as divine speech. Fix: anchor a human context, e.g. 'أَوْحَيْنَا لِلْمُدِيرِ بِالْحَلِّ فِي الِاجْتِمَاعِ' (We suggested the solution to the manager in the meeting).

subject: حرم_2:#4
detail: 'حَرَّمْنَا' is the Quranic divine 'We made unlawful' (e.g. وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا), and humans declaring something haram is theologically sensitive. Fix: make the human self-restriction explicit, e.g. 'حَرَّمْنَا عَلَى أَنْفُسِنَا التَّدْخِينَ فِي الْبَيْتِ' (We forbade ourselves smoking in the house / Zabranili smo sebi pušenje u kući).

subject: وكل_5:#6
detail: 'تَوَكَّلْنَا عَلَى اللَّهِ' is a near-verbatim reordering of the Quranic phrase 'عَلَى اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْنَا' (7:89, 10:85). Fix: e.g. 'تَوَكَّلْنَا عَلَى صَدِيقِنَا فِي تَرْتِيبِ السَّفَرِ' (We relied on our friend to arrange the trip / Oslonili smo se na prijatelja u organizaciji puta).

subject: كتم_1:#0

subject: بلو_1:#0

subject: حقق_1:#0

subject: حقق_1:#1
detail: حَقَّتْ لَهُ الْجَائِزَةُ is stilted/unidiomatic in MSA (one says اسْتَحَقَّ الْجَائِزَةَ, which is Form X). Use a natural Form I usage, e.g. حَقَّ لَهُ أَنْ يَفْخَرَ بِنَجَاحِهِ 'He had every right to be proud of his success' / 'Imao je pravo da se ponosi svojim uspjehom.'

subject: حلل_4:#0

subject: حقق_1:#3

detail: أَغْرَقَ means drown/flood/drench, not 'soak' a garment (that is اُنْقُعْ or اِغْمِسْ), so the English is wrong and the usage is forced. Fix: أَغْرِقِ الْفَطِيرَةَ بِالْعَسَلِ 'Drench the pancake in honey.' / 'Prelij palačinku obilno medom.'

subject: قلب_7:#5
detail: انْقَلَبُوا مِنَ الضَّحِكِ is not an established MSA idiom; on its own it reads as 'they turned/returned' or 'they turned over', not 'rolled over laughing'. Fix: انْقَلَبُوا عَلَى ظُهُورِهِمْ مِنَ الضَّحِكِ 'They fell onto their backs laughing.' / 'Pali su na leđa od smijeha.'

subject: قلب_7:#6
detail: Children rolling around on grass is يَتَقَلَّبُونَ (Form V) or يَتَدَحْرَجُونَ. Form VII انْقَلَبَ means a single flip or overturn, used mostly for objects, so it is forced here. Fix with Form VII: انْقَلَبَ الْقَارِبُ الصَّغِيرُ فِي الْبُحَيْرَةِ / or for hum: الْأَطْفَالُ يَنْقَلِبُونَ عَلَى ظُهُورِهِمْ مِنَ الضَّحِكِ 'The children fall onto their backs laughing.'

subject: قلب_7:#7
detail: انْقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَى ... most naturally reads 'you turned against ...', so the sentence is ambiguous and the usage forced. EN 'rolled over' and BS 'prevrnuli ste se' (toppled over) also do not match each other. Fix: انْقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَى ظُهُورِكُمْ فَوْقَ الرِّمَالِ 'You fell onto your backs on the sand.' / 'Pali ste na leđa na pijesku.'

subject: أفك_1:imperative:anta
detail: skipped by policy: the imperative اِئْفِكْ commands the learner to lie

subject: عدو_8:imperative:antum
detail: skipped by policy: the imperative اِعْتَدُوا commands the learner to transgress or attack

subject: منن_1:#1
detail: Bosnian 'prigovara za svoje poklone' is unnatural and reads as 'complains about his gifts'; use 'Plemenit čovjek ne prebacuje drugima svoje poklone.' (gloss: 'prebacuje')

subject: منن_1:#3
detail: Bosnian 'Ne prigovaraju za svoje davanje' is unnatural and misleading (sounds like 'they don't complain about their giving'); use 'Ne prebacuju drugima ono što su dali.' (gloss: 'prebacuju')

subject: صدق_1:#1
detail: صدقوا في وعدهم means they kept/were true to their promise; Bosnian 'Bili su iskreni u svom obećanju' (sincere in their promise) is off and mismatches the English; use 'Održali su svoje obećanje.' (gloss: 'održali su')

subject: عدو_8:#3
detail: اعتدينا على وقت الراحة ('we encroached on rest time') is an unnatural collocation in Arabic, English and Bosnian ('zadrli smo u vrijeme odmora'); replace with a natural sentence, e.g. لَا نَعْتَدِي عَلَى أَحَدٍ

subject: عدو_8:#4
detail: On its own, مَوْقِفِ الْجِيرَانِ reads first as 'the neighbours' stance/position', not their parking spot (that would need مَوْقِفِ سَيَّارَةِ ...). The Bosnian 'Zauzeli smo' ('we took') drops the sense of wrongful transgression in اعتدى. The sentence also has the learner's 'we' admitting a wrong. Suggested fix: مَا اعْتَدَيْنَا عَلَى حَقِّ جِيرَانِنَا / 'We did not violate our neighbours' rights.' / 'Nismo nasrnuli na prava svojih komšija.'

subject: عدو_8:#5
detail: Vowelling error: hamzat al-wasl in اِعْتَدَيْنَا is marked with kasra mid-sentence after مَا, where it is elided (mā-ʿtadaynā); write اعْتَدَيْنَا with a bare alif (or ٱ). Otherwise sentence, glosses and translations are correct.
